request: Give Vaemyr the fuller, source-checked profile treatment.

scope.limits: This is discovery across overlapping caches, not exhaustive reading of all messages. Selected complete quest exchanges, narrator rulings/endings, the non-explicit Tower reconciliation and later disappearance statements are read. Raw transcripts, controller data, intimate material, unreviewed attachments and protected sources remain external.

decisions: Vaemyr remains the same existing player character with original artwork, relationship map, route and seven chapter identities. Fourteen old section targets and seven old chapter targets remain; thirteen old section narratives/evidence panels are exact.

Ten additions restore practical magic, magical compulsion, imperfect behavior, race humor, Alavara’s actual sacrifice, the proposed Rahu trial, Squiddy’s completed rescue, harvest work, study, the battle departure, reconciliation and later missing reports. No new NPC/generic creature record or image is created.

The throne narrator explicitly imposes the anger curse. It contextualizes Vaemyr’s behavior without converting the false vision into divine fact or erasing his rough treatment and objection to healing Empty.

Vaemyr presses Alavara and takes the first blade. Her sorrowful acceptance is not a wish to die. The narrator’s disappearance/portal ending and unknown heroism remain distinct from Vaemyr’s question about whether the task is done. He does not receive sole credit for the company’s action.

Gudlaug and Beefy Boy win the race. Vaemyr’s puns, pride, rejection of whipping, repeated swats and belated concern for his exhausted wolf remain together. His posture is not rewritten as perfect kindness.

Diplomatic requests coexist with a willingness to assist covert action and later sharp questioning. Hildethrax offers a long path and Vaemyr promises to return; neither completed Rahu standing nor final resolution of Swift’s case is invented.

The quest explicitly returns Squiddy alive and well. Vaemyr’s injuries, irritation with Krone, petty amusement at Carmen, practical help and return to study remain. The harvest exchange is an offered lesson, not a demonstrated completed one.

The primary battle sequence corrects one earlier synthesis: Dale’s fall and the fight-together commitment precede Olokun’s killing blow. All original direct quote blocks and quoted wording survive. No permanent death or later status is inferred from a historic fall.

The quest explicitly has Vaemyr leave to search for Wren and Olokun’s remains. In the later Tower scene his explanation emphasizes Wren; it does not overwrite the quest. Their observed reconciliation preserves his apology and Wren’s refusal to change her willingness to risk herself. No invented search itinerary or complete cure of their disagreement.

Arjahn is asked to officiate an intended marriage, then later remembers a proposal plan. No actual proposal, engagement or wedding is confirmed here. Later companions call Vaemyr missing; Olokun’s Astral Sea guess is explicitly not a location finding. Scribonia’s later description of his first students stays attributed.

Five Vaemyr directory/related summaries and two type labels change; no other world structures, event dates/importance/calendar adjustments, maps, quotes, people roles, media/261 previews or complete private-payload bytes change.

editorialDeltas.introBefore:
Vaemyr often appears to be the reasonable person in a dangerous room, but reasonableness is only the surface of his character. His recurring question is what responsibility becomes once he chooses to care about another person. He is cautious because promises have consequences, not because he lacks the courage to make them.

That concern makes him practical without making him cold. When Olokun wants to keep helping vulnerable commoners during a dangerous journey, Vaemyr says that he wants to help too, then asks whether the company can actually keep them safe. He wants the company to plan for the rescued people’s safety after bringing them out of immediate danger.
editorialDeltas.introAfter:
Vaemyr is a winged tiefling spellcaster who explores dangerous places, studies with other mages and tries to get his companions home alive. He carries a grimoire, uses protective and temporal magic, and is often the one asking the party to slow down. He can also be proud, irritable, funny and badly frightened. His first meeting with Goo requires an apology; a public race exposes both his competitiveness and his affection for a tired wolf.

When he chooses to care for someone, Vaemyr takes the obligations seriously. Asked to help endangered commoners, he wants to know how the company will keep them safe after the rescue. With Olokun and Wren, that careful thinking becomes deeply personal. It helps him remain beside them in danger, and it can also become an attempt to decide what risks another person is allowed to take.
editorialDeltas.roadsBefore:
The Roads and the November battle

On 13 November 2024, Vaemyr returns from the Roads and collapses into Wren’s embrace. He tells her, “For you, Wren, I would make any sacrifice.” Three days later, Olokun’s death nearly breaks his resolve. He forces himself onward: “Not. Yet.”

Then Dale falls, and Wren begins to despair. Bloodied and covered in ash, Vaemyr mouths the commitment that brings his careful thinking into shared danger:

I love you. Let's fight together.Vaemyr, 16 November 2024
editorialDeltas.roadsAfter:
The Roads and the November battle

On 13 November 2024, Vaemyr returns from the Roads and collapses into Wren’s embrace. He tells her, “For you, Wren, I would make any sacrifice.” Three days later, Dale falls, and Wren begins to despair. Bloodied and covered in ash, Vaemyr mouths his commitment:

I love you. Let's fight together.Vaemyr, 16 November 2024

Later in the same battle, Olokun’s death nearly breaks his resolve. He remembers the friend who welcomed him to Prima, then hears Wren and forces himself onward: “Not. Yet.”
